question: Does the candidate acquisition logic (incumbent hysteresis + 3s ambiguity timeout + 5-frame sustained gesture) beat shipped on ≥30 HUMAN-VERIFIED cases, per the D-026 gate?

verifiedCorpus.verificationMethod: devin-visual-v1: per-case render (region + true-target + other tracks) visually reviewed; every verdict carries a written note; rejects include 2 graphic title cards, 2 non-pickleball sports scenes (multi-sport reel), 1 out-of-domain lobby bokeh, 1 ambiguous track binding

results_locked_test_one_shot_n5.protocol: parameters frozen on dev BEFORE this run; shipped and candidate each executed exactly once; no iteration afterward

decision: PROMOTED (D-027). Candidate dominates or ties every measured dimension on dev n=31 (correct locks 16→22, false gestures 2→0, on-target .543→.612, lock rate .806→1.0, cost +111ms median) and wins/ties all dimensions on the one-shot held-out n=5 (locks 4/5→5/5, on-target .553→.639). Implemented in GuidedCaptureViewController.swift (sustained gesture + ambiguity timeout) and ApplePoseProvider.swift (incumbent hysteresis). TS replay 'shipped' now tracks the promoted semantics; pre-promotion behavior preserved as 'legacy' variant with regression tests.
residualRisks: lockCorrectRate 0.71 on dev: remaining wrong locks concentrate in crowd/huddle cases where the machine-proposed 'region' sits on a bystander cluster — partly a case-construction artifact (proposals put regions on ANY stable track, including spectators). Product regions are user-tapped court positions.

ambiguity_timeout locks the closest occupant; in a genuinely contested region this can still pick a partner standing on the exact spot — the sustained-gesture path remains the intended resolution when the user cooperates.
verified n=36 total; slices are thin (e.g. only 4 solo/two_player cases). Keep verifying from the queue.
physical iPhone behavior (live jitter, frame drops) not measured — replay uses batch extraction.
artifacts: datasets/ta-bench/results/ (dev runs n=31 all variants; locked_test one-shots), datasets/ta-bench/cases.json (36 verified with notes)
